title: Montréal
intro: Walk and talk, browse beautiful little shops, eat very well, and linger over coffee and dessert. One relaxed route each day, with nearby extras when you feel like it.

hotel.name: Le Mount Stephen
hotel.label: Your chosen base
hotel.description: A historic mansion paired with modern rooms, plus Bar George downstairs. The most overtly grand choice.
hotel.beds: Deluxe Two Queen Room · request two actual queen beds

booking: Le Mount Stephen is the selected hotel, not a confirmed booking. Reserve the Deluxe Two Queen Room, Leméac for Saturday lunch, and Monarque’s brasserie for Saturday dinner.
assumptions: Assumes driving from Boston and sharing one room with two beds. All times are Eastern. Recheck hours before leaving.

places.name: La Banquise
places.description: The flexible late-arrival poutine stop. Keep it casual tonight and save the nice meal for Saturday.
places.note: Check late kitchen hours before leaving the hotel.

places.name: St-Viateur Bagel
places.description: The original wood-fired bagel shop. Get a hot sesame bagel and watch the baking.
places.note: A quick start, not a sit-down brunch.

places.name: Café Olimpico
places.description: Espresso and a lively neighborhood crowd. Pause here together after bagels rather than treating coffee as another quick errand.
places.note: Use the original Saint-Viateur location.

places.name: Bref
places.description: A bright gallery-boutique of ceramics, prints, and limited-edition design objects.
places.note: Saturday and Sunday 11 AM–5 PM on the contact page.

places.name: LVNEA
places.description: Locally made botanical perfumes: resins, woods, unusual atmospheric scents.
places.note: Entrance on Casgrain; published weekend hours 11 AM–6 PM.

places.name: Librairie Drawn & Quarterly
places.mapQuery: Librairie Drawn & Quarterly, 176 Rue Bernard Ouest
places.description: Art books, graphic novels, and good things to pick up and show each other.
places.note: On Bernard, by Bref and the record shops.

places.name: H Parfums
places.description: A polished niche-perfume boutique with independent houses to compare.
places.note: Saturday 10 AM–5 PM; Sunday noon–5 PM.

places.name: Schwartz’s Deli
places.description: Montréal smoked meat, mustard, and a pickle. Order medium-fat.
places.note: Use takeaway if the sit-down queue is long.

places.name: Habitat 67
places.description: A genuinely unusual stacked-housing experiment. A guided visit has more substance than a distant glance.
places.note: The 2026 tour calendar reaches Nov 22. Saturday slots are unverified; internal access requires a tour. Separate taxi trip across the water.

places.name: L’Express
places.description: A classic French bistro with a serious cellar and late service.
places.note: A dinner alternative to Monarque. Reserve by phone: +1 514 845-5333.

places.name: Cloakroom Bar
places.mapQuery: Cloakroom Bar, 2175 Rue de la Montagne
places.description: An intimate, no-menu cocktail bar that builds a drink around the flavors you like.
places.note: 25 seats, no reservations. Ask the price before ordering rare spirits.

places.name: Crew Collective & Café
places.description: A spectacular former bank turned café. A proper place to sit, have coffee, and talk while enjoying the architecture.
places.note: A public café, not just coworking space. Tables can be busy; seating is not guaranteed.

places.name: Place d’Armes & Notre-Dame
places.description: The blue-and-gold basilica interior is much more striking than a quick look at the façade.
places.note: Daytime adult entry starts at CAD 16 + tax; AURA starts at CAD 37 + tax. Sunday sightseeing is 12:30–4 PM.

places.name: L’Empreinte coopérative
places.description: Québec-made ceramics, glass, jewelry, and artisan objects in an actual makers’ cooperative.
places.note: 88 Saint-Paul Est. Confirm seasonal November opening times.

places.name: Rue Saint-Paul → Old Port
places.description: Stone streets, river views, little passages, and a long waterfront promenade.
places.note: The exposed river edge is windy; the streets are an easy shorter loop.

places.name: Olive et Gourmando
places.mapQuery: Olive et Gourmando, 351 Rue Saint-Paul Ouest
places.description: A cozy old-city café for excellent sandwiches, baked goods, and a proper lunch.
places.note: 351 Saint-Paul Ouest; published weekends 8 AM–5 PM. Takeaway avoids a brunch wait.

places.name: Leméac
places.description: A more polished Outremont bistro for a long lunch or proper dinner.
places.note: Weekend brunch/lunch 10 AM–3 PM; dinner 5–11 PM. Reserve.

places.name: Pâtisserie Au Kouign-Amann
places.mapQuery: Pâtisserie Au Kouign-Amann, 316 Avenue du Mont-Royal Est
places.description: A slice of caramelized, buttery kouign-amann. Split one while it is warm.
places.note: Saturday option. Tastet lists Sunday closed.

places.name: North Star Machines à Piastres
places.mapQuery: North Star Machines à Piastres, 3908 Boulevard Saint-Laurent
places.description: Vintage pinball, a drink, and a little friendly competition.
places.note: Opposite the Schwartz’s stretch; machine noise, not a quiet lounge. Confirm hours.

places.name: Bota Bota
places.description: A floating hot-and-cold spa with river views. Keep this as an optional spa outing if you specifically want a quiet session.
places.note: Silence is required on the boat, so this is a weaker fit for a conversation-focused afternoon. Confirm conversation-permitted areas before booking. Swimsuit needed.

places.name: Cité Mémoire night walk
places.description: Local stories projected onto real buildings after dark. Try a couple on an evening walk.
places.note: Operator lists reopened scenes Wednesday–Sunday after nightfall. Check the current app map.

places.name: Ex-Voto
places.description: A well-curated mix of local clothing, ceramics, stationery, and home objects.
places.note: Pair with État de choc; both sit on the Saint-Laurent approach to Little Italy.

places.name: Bernie Beigne
places.description: Big, fluffy doughnuts and playful flavors. The fun sweet stop in this cluster.
places.note: Bernard Ouest. Check current hours and go before sell-outs.

places.name: Les chocolats de Chloé
places.mapQuery: Les chocolats de Chloé, 546 Avenue Duluth Est
places.description: Handmade chocolates, caramels, and crunchy chocolate-coated sponge toffee.
places.note: 546 Duluth Est; Saturday 11 AM–6 PM, Sunday 11 AM–5 PM.

places.name: Monarque · Brasserie
places.description: The upgraded dinner pick: a handsome room, polished service, and ambitious French cooking.
places.note: Book the brasserie, not the separate four-course dining room. Saturday service from 5 PM.

places.name: Chez Potier
places.description: The refined pastry stop: individual cakes, chocolate work, macarons, and beautiful seasonal desserts.
places.note: 630 Wellington; weekends 8 AM–5 PM. Excellent for pastries, but seating is limited: this is not the main long café break.

places.name: Bar George
places.description: Carved wood, stained glass, cocktails, and a grand mansion setting. Get a drink and the café gourmand.
places.note: The current menu lists five mini desserts for CAD 20. Bar seating is walk-in.

places.name: Ratafia
places.description: Inventive plated desserts with wine or cocktails. This is the dessert destination, not just a bakery stop.
places.note: Evening only, Tuesday–Saturday from 5 PM; closed Sunday. It replaces the evening plan, not a quick daytime detour.

places.name: État de choc
places.description: Bean-to-bar chocolates, tasting bars, and gifts that are actually worth bringing home.
places.note: 6466 Saint-Laurent; Saturday 10 AM–5 PM, Sunday 11 AM–5 PM.

days.label: Friday night
days.title: Check in. A drink in the mansion.
days.summary: Le Mount Stephen is the base. Keep the arrival night close to home.

blocks.title: Le Mount Stephen · settle in
blocks.text: Check into the Deluxe Two Queen Room, leave the car, and drop your bags. Let reception know you will arrive at night.

blocks.title: Bar George · first drink, something good to eat
blocks.text: Walk downstairs into the historic mansion for a cocktail and a proper first-night bite. Bar bites run until 10 PM; if you arrive later, eat on the way and keep this to a drink.
blocks.note: Friday bar service runs late. Dining room reservations do not reserve bar seats.

nearby.text: If you need a later dinner: this classic French bistro lists service until 1 AM. Taxi there and check last kitchen orders.

days.label: Saturday
days.title: Perfume, ceramics, a long lunch.
days.summary: Mile End and Outremont for independent shops and a polished lunch. Chocolate on Duluth, then a proper dinner and a cocktail.

blocks.title: Olimpico · coffee and a slow start
blocks.text: Taxi to the original Saint-Viateur café. Sit with an espresso and ease into the neighborhood. No need to rush into another activity.

nearby.text: One worthwhile casual exception: a warm sesame bagel from the original wood-fired shop. A quick cultural taste, not today’s main meal.

blocks.title: Bref · ceramics and independent design
blocks.text: Walk along Bernard to browse small-run ceramics, prints, and design objects. This is one of the shops to make time for.

nearby.text: Graphic novels, art books, and independent publishing, a short walk along Bernard.

blocks.title: H Parfums · try something unfamiliar
blocks.text: Walk south toward Laurier and take your time with niche fragrances. Try a few on skin and let them develop while you walk.

blocks.title: Leméac · the nice lunch
blocks.text: Reserve a table for a proper French bistro lunch. Make this a long, seated meal rather than a sandwich eaten in a queue. Allow CAD 55–90 each before tax and tip, depending on drinks.
blocks.note: Weekend brunch/lunch is published as 10 AM–3 PM. Reserve.

blocks.title: LVNEA · botanical perfume
blocks.text: Head east through the neighborhood to the Saint-Viateur boutique. Woods, resins, and atmospheric botanical scents made locally. Slow browsing is the activity.
blocks.note: Entrance on Casgrain. Published weekend hours 11 AM–6 PM.

blocks.title: Chloé · handmade chocolates and a Duluth stroll
blocks.text: Take a taxi down to Duluth, or walk if you feel like a longer stretch. Pick out handmade chocolates, then wander Duluth and Saint-Denis at your own pace.

nearby.text: For another distinctly Montréal pastry: the buttery kouign-amann. This is a detour toward Mont-Royal, not right next door.

blocks.title: Hotel break · leave room for dinner
blocks.text: Taxi back to Le Mount Stephen, put down your purchases, and have a real break. No need to fill every spare hour.

blocks.title: Monarque · brasserie dinner
blocks.text: Book the brasserie, rather than the formal tasting-menu dining room. A polished dinner with room to choose your spend. Allow CAD 85–130 each before tax and tip. Order dessert if it catches your eye.

nearby.text: The dessert-focused alternative: plated desserts and wine in Little Italy. Choose this instead of the dinner/cocktail sequence, not as another cross-city stop. Open Saturday evening; closed Sunday.

blocks.title: Cloakroom · one excellent cocktail
blocks.text: Taxi back toward the hotel for a small, intimate cocktail bar. Let the bartender build something around flavors you like. Walk home afterward. Skip it if dinner becomes the evening.
blocks.note: Bar George downstairs at the hotel is the easy backup if Cloakroom is full.

days.label: Sunday
days.title: Old streets, a grand café, and very good pastry.
days.summary: Old Montréal, Place d’Armes, Notre-Dame, and the river. Then an easy afternoon of chocolate and shops. Leave at 6 PM.

blocks.title: Check out, then Crew · breakfast under the bank ceiling
blocks.text: Leave your bags and car with the hotel, then taxi to Crew Collective & Café. Take a table for breakfast and coffee in the former Royal Bank hall. Stay awhile.
blocks.note: Confirm after-checkout parking and luggage storage with Le Mount Stephen.

blocks.title: L’Empreinte · Québec-made craft on Saint-Paul
blocks.text: Walk the old streets and browse the cooperative for locally made ceramics, jewelry, and objects. This is the Old Montréal boutique stop worth prioritizing.
blocks.note: Seasonal Sunday opening needs confirmation. If it opens later, return after Notre-Dame.

blocks.title: Old Port · a short river walk
blocks.text: Walk down to the waterfront for the change of scale and river views. Keep it short if the wind is unpleasant, and spend longer on the sheltered old streets instead.

blocks.title: Place d’Armes & Notre-Dame · the main sight
blocks.text: Return to the square, then go inside the basilica. This is the dramatic interior that earns its place in the plan. Sunday sightseeing is 12:30–4 PM. Daytime entry starts at CAD 16 plus tax; AURA is a separate evening ticket.

blocks.title: Chez Potier · a proper pastry stop
blocks.text: Walk to Wellington for refined individual pastries, chocolates, and a light savory lunch. Choose what looks best in the case, plus something for the drive. A few seats only, so this is not the long café hangout.

nearby.text: Olive et Gourmando is the sit-down sandwich and lunch alternative, closer to Saint-Paul. Choose it before the pastry stop if you want a bigger meal.

blocks.title: État de choc · chocolate worth taking home
blocks.text: Taxi north to the Saint-Laurent chocolate specialist. Browse the bean-to-bar selection and pick out a few unusual bars or bonbons.

blocks.title: Ex-Voto · the last browse
blocks.text: Walk along Saint-Laurent for design objects, jewelry, and small gifts. Leave time to sit for a coffee rather than trying to squeeze in another neighborhood.
blocks.note: This is the northbound shopping detour. The skating option below replaces this whole afternoon detour, if open.

blocks.title: Back to Le Mount Stephen · bags and car
blocks.text: Taxi back, collect the bags and car, and pick up a takeaway meal if needed. Arrange car retrieval before heading back.

blocks.title: Leave for Boston
blocks.text: Drive home. Expect a late-night arrival around midnight or later with stops and the border. Check live navigation and the US entry queue before leaving.

practical.title: Book the anchors
practical.text: Le Mount Stephen: Deluxe Two Queen Room. Leméac: Saturday 12:30 PM. Monarque: Saturday 7 PM, brasserie. These are selections, not confirmed reservations.

practical.title: Time to talk
practical.text: Treat the times as a relaxed order, except the meal bookings and Sunday departure. Skip extras when a good conversation, shop, or dessert deserves longer.

practical.title: Getting around
practical.text: Walk within each neighborhood, taxi between clusters. Prices are planning allowances in CAD before tax and tip. Hotel estimate: USD 300–450 per person for both nights sharing one room, including estimated room taxes, excluding parking; not a live quote.

practical.title: The return drive
practical.text: Leave Sunday at 6 PM. Confirm hotel parking after checkout, check navigation and the Highgate Springs border queue, and expect a late-night Boston arrival.

neighborhoods.name: Mile End & Outremont
neighborhoods.subtitle: Coffee, independent design, perfume, and a polished bistro. Your Saturday morning cluster.

neighborhoods.name: The Plateau
neighborhoods.subtitle: Lunch, handmade chocolates, a great pastry, and a short game of pinball. Walk between these stops.

neighborhoods.name: Old Montréal & the river
neighborhoods.subtitle: The main afternoon and Sunday cluster. Chez Potier is at the western edge; Habitat 67 needs a taxi across the water.

neighborhoods.name: Golden Square Mile
neighborhoods.subtitle: Two polished evening stops near the downtown hotels. A taxi transfer from Old Montréal.

neighborhoods.name: Little Italy · the dessert detour
neighborhoods.subtitle: North of Mile End, so treat this as a separate cluster. Ratafia is an evening destination; chocolate and shopping work in the day.

hotels.name: Le Germain Montréal
hotels.label: Easy default
hotels.description: Refined, comfortable, and central. The cleanest shared-room choice.

hotels.name: Hôtel William Gray
hotels.label: Best old-city atmosphere
hotels.description: Stone architecture, contemporary rooms, and a real hotel living room. Best if you want the hotel to feel part of the trip.
hotels.beds: Confirm a two-bed category; many rooms are kings.

hotels.name: Le Mount Stephen
hotels.label: Your chosen base
hotels.description: A historic mansion paired with modern rooms, plus Bar George downstairs. The most overtly grand choice.
hotels.beds: Deluxe Two Queen Room · request two actual queen beds

hotels.name: Hôtel Nelligan
hotels.label: Warm, romantic old stone
hotels.description: Brick, beams, and a cozy Old Montréal base. A good counterpoint to the modern downtown hotels.
hotels.beds: Confirm the current two-bed room category directly.

extras.label: Sunday afternoon swap · only if confirmed open
extras.title: Esplanade Tranquille · skate under the lights
extras.text: A fun shared activity, with a pavilion for warming up. Replace the Little Italy shopping detour with skating; do not add another transfer to the day. The operator still lists the rink as closed with reopening planned for mid-November 2026, so check the live page before committing. Admission is normally free; rentals cost extra.
